intent: generate new themed assets, not edit reference pixels
common:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Unity 2D side-view pixel-art modular castle wall sprites, for a difficult Jump King-like game on a cheerful XP-style sky backdrop.
Primary request: design ONE complete original architectural theme as an eight-piece sprite atlas. Make the design striking and genuinely distinct in silhouette, material, construction and ornamental vocabulary. Reference images convey only coarse pixel-art readability and the eight-part module concept: do not trace their outlines or replicate their block placement.
Layout: square canvas, exactly four columns and two rows, eight separate tall slender wall pieces on real transparent alpha, generous empty gutters. Top row LEFT wall: 1 top termination with ledge pointing RIGHT toward gameplay space, 2 seamless vertical repeat body, 3 bottom foot with ledge RIGHT, 4 broken-through body with a big EMPTY hole. Bottom row RIGHT wall: the same four roles with architecture and ledges facing LEFT. No labels or diagram arrows.
Modularity: every piece uses the same straight outer structural spine for its side and the same cross-section at joins. The middle repeat has a flat cut at both ends, NO decorative caps at joins; make its top edge and bottom edge match. Top and bottom modules connect to this cross-section. Broken module keeps matching end sections and an actual transparent passage in the middle, not merely a crack filled with background.
Pixel style: chunky deliberate 1990s game sprite pixel clusters, apparent 64x144 logical pixels per module enlarged nearest-neighbor; sharp square stair-step edges, limited intentional color ramps, thick dark outlines, restrained 3-tone shadows. Simple readable forms, not detailed painting, not 3D render, no blurry shading, no bloom, no antialiasing. Flat front-facing side-view platform collision silhouette, not isometric. Largest keys/blocks around half the height of a stout 30-pixel-tall player; entire wall piece around four to five player heights.
Keep recognizable keyboard/computer ancestry integrated into CASTLE ARCHITECTURE: some blank beveled square and rectangular keycap blocks, tiny simple key symbols at most, no legible words. Dominant architectural style is specified below.
Avoid grass, soil, vines, plants, scenery, sky, floor plane, characters, logos, watermarks, solid black backdrops, checkerboard backdrops, all perspective planes, cast ground shadows. Exterior and gaps must be true alpha. All eight pieces fully visible with clear separation.

variants.name: 백색 고딕
variants.theme: THEME 1 — PORCELAIN KEY CATHEDRAL. Ivory glazed ceramic and pale limestone architecture, muted ultramarine in narrow pointed arch recesses, tiny antique-gold hinge accents. Outer spine is a very slim fluted cathedral buttress, repeated pointed window niches, chunky pale keycap masonry on inner edge. Top ledge uses stepped organ-key battlements and a small pointed turret; bottom has a two-step plinth. Give it a light elegant cathedral silhouette with distinct negative space under corbels. Broken piece exposes porcelain thickness and one snapped golden tie bar, large open passage. NOT black computer housings or orange wires. Palette cream, warm beige, dusty blue, deep navy outlines, sparse dull gold.

variants.theme: THEME 2 — OBSIDIAN SWITCH FORTRESS. Massive angular charcoal-violet basalt slabs interlocked like mechanical keyboard switch housings; strong jagged stepped silhouette and broad reinforced bands. variants.theme: THEME 3 — TERRACOTTA KEY BASTION. Warm fired-red brick fortification, staggered horizontal brick courses, pale ochre mortar pixels, chunky cream ceramic keycaps inset sparsely like arrow-slit shutters.
